name: Muzli
one_liner: Curated design-inspiration feed delivered as a new-tab browser extension, with collections, search and a color tool.
what_it_offers: A free extension for Chrome/Chromium, Edge, Safari (Mac) and Firefox (experimental) that turns each new tab into a feed drawn from 200+ design sources, mixed with editorial picks. The wider ecosystem adds roughly 60 themed inspiration collections (landing pages, UI/UX, branding, portfolios and more), Muzli Search, the Muzli Colors palette generator and color-names index, a creative-tools directory, an asset store, designer profiles, a blog/Medium publication and a design job board. Muzli Pro adds an ad-free feed, Muzli Web (the feed in any browser, including mobile), custom hero content, premium collections, 3 nominations/month and cross-device sync. A contact-sales Enterprise plan offers unlimited seats and managed browser deployment.
tech_stack: Nuxt (Vue) site; Pro billing via Lemon Squeezy
portfolio_fit_reason: A free, constantly refreshed inspiration feed. It includes a dedicated portfolio collection and a palette tool, so it's a good daily source of references, but it produces no code or assets.
client_ok_note: Muzli's Terms allow personal use only and ban republishing. Featured work belongs to its creators, and palettes come with no explicit license.
best_use_for_portfolio: Before designing, open Muzli's portfolio and landing-page collections and save 5 to 10 references for the hero, project grid and case-study pages. Try out an accent palette in Muzli Colors, then hand the screenshots and hex values to a coding agent as the visual brief.
tier_reason: A free, constantly refreshed inspiration feed with a dedicated portfolio collection and a palette tool. A strong daily reference, though it produces no code or assets.
pick_over_overlaps: Use it for passive daily browsing, not targeted research. Awwwards is better when you need to search by technique or category.
score_rationale: Broad, constantly refreshed and free inspiration that fits both passive daily discovery and targeted pattern research (e.g., its landing-page and portfolio collections). It doesn't produce code or reusable assets, and much of it is aggregated from other galleries, so it informs rather than builds.
free_tier: Free forever, no trial or card: the extension, new-tab feed from 200+ sources, daily editorial picks, personalization, Muzli Colors, Search, profiles and work uploads, inspiration collections, the tools directory, blog, jobs and 1 lifetime project nomination. Limits: the feed has ads, and there's no Muzli Web or premium collections.
paid_entry_label: Muzli Pro $9/mo billed monthly ($60/yr billed annually = $5/mo; list price $90/yr)
paid_top_label: Muzli Pro Lifetime $350 one-time. All Pro plans share an identical feature set. Enterprise (unlimited seats, managed deployment) is contact-sales with no public price.
commercial_use_license: Not licensed for reuse. Muzli's Terms (muz.li/terms/) say Muzli and/or its licensors own the IP in site material. Access is for your own personal use, and republishing, reproducing, redistributing or sub-licensing material is prohibited. Featured work belongs to its original creators. Use it for inspiration only. Palettes are just color values, but the terms grant no explicit license.
agent_friendly: Partial. Publishes https://muz.li/llms.txt, llms-full.txt and a machine-readable pricing.md (last updated 2026-08-17) that an agent can read for product and pricing facts. No public API docs, MCP server or npm package; the inspiration content sits behind Nuxt pages.
maintenance_signal: Very active. Chrome Web Store: v33.1.9 updated Sept 10, 2026, rated 4.5 from 833 ratings, 400,000 Chrome users. llms.txt claims 800,000+ total users, 'approaching 900,000'. pricing.md last updated 2026-08-17. The Medium publication RSS shows posts on Sept 10-11, 2026. (The inspiration page's 'Last updated' date renders as the current day, so it isn't a reliable signal.)
caveats: Replaces your new-tab page, which some users won't want, and the free feed has ads. Content is aggregated from other galleries (overlap with Dribbble and Behance), and shot-style work can favor pretty over shippable. No self-serve team plan (Enterprise is contact-sales only). No partial refunds. Firefox support is experimental and there's no mobile app (Muzli Web is Pro-only). The terms restrict use to personal use with no reuse.
